html:
Turkana Boy is the nearly complete skeleton of a youth of the species Homo erectus, or Homo ergaster, found in 1984 by Kamoya Kimeu of Richard Leakey's team at Nariokotome, west of Lake Turkana in Kenya.

He lived about 1.5 million years ago and died young. His long legs and narrow hips showed that early humans had a modern body shape for walking and running in open country.

He is one of many finds around Lake Turkana, where the Leakey family and Kenyan fossil hunters worked for decades. Fossils from Kenya and Tanzania, among them Olduvai and Laetoli, show East Africa as the main stage of human evolution. The skeleton is kept in Nairobi.
